text:
maya: heads-up: seeing sustained 95th/99th token latency increases in us-west-2 for route /v1/generate since 03:12 UTC, correlates with 2 GPU nodes in pool-gpu-a flapping
jon: saw same, request queue depth jumped, we started shedding at the admission layer
maya: current behavior is FIFO per-pool. when nodes die, tails get long and important tenant jobs are blocked
sasha: can we switch to priority per-route? risk starving batch jobs though
liam: proposal: per-route queues + weighted priority, with capacity tokens per-pool. admission control checks tokens before enqueue
maya: sketch:
```yaml
queues:
  per_route: true
  priorities:
    - name: realtime
      weight: 100
    - name: background
      weight: 10
capacity:
  pool_tokens: 1024
admission: token_check
```
eva: also consider dynamic aging to prevent starvation: increase weight by time_in_queue
jon: another idea: fallback routing — if route's pool saturated, route can failover to cheaper quantized variant in other region (with perf penalty)
maya: region failover complicates data residency; can't for some enterprise tenants
sasha: can we do admission that enforces tenant fairness + route SLAs? i.e., reserved min tokens per-tenant + burst pool
liam: cost note: weighted priority makes tails better but increases GPU utilization slightly, keep an eye on cost-per-token
infra-bot: alert: pool-gpu-a node3 removed from pool at 03:18 UTC (restarts=4) — https://infra/alert/1234
maya: next steps: 1) quick rollout of per-route queuing experiment to canary 10% traffic 2) add aging param 3) simulate burst w/chaos
jon: +1, i'll create a PR with config toggle
sasha: +1, add test cases for fairness
liam: I'll run cost simulation and post numbers
maya: thanks. if anyone sees 99th > 1.2s, ping me
eva: :thumbsup:
